medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
Stanford takes pride in its highly diverse and exceptionally qualified student body and welcomes all individuals and groups to pursue a career in medicine. To view programs and groups committed to supporting these efforts including the summer Leadership in Health Disparities Program (LHDP), please visit the Office of Diversity in Medical Education website at https://med.stanford.edu/odme

For information related to ODME programming, contact Mark Gutierrez, Director of ODME at marz@stanford.edu.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence:
Leaves of Absence are granted at the discretion of the School of Medicine, and are granted for a maximum of one calendar year. Leaves requested for a longer period are approved only in exceptional circumstances. Extension requests must be made to the Committee on Performance, Professionalism and Promotion before the expiration of the original Leave of Absence.

For additional information please visit:  https://med.stanford.edu/md/mdhandbook/section-3-9-leaves-of-absenceand-reinstatement.html
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
The Stanford Medical Student Association (SMSA) functions as a local liaison for national medical student organizations and addresses issues that affect Stanford medical students and the School of Medicine community. SMSA sponsors a wide range of scientific, political, social, and health-oriented activities for students, and provides monetary support for community service projects.
 
A list of student organizations and activities can be found at the SMSA website. 
https://med.stanford.edu/smsa.html
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The school is located on the 8,180 acre campus of Stanford University (second largest university complex in the world) and is situated in Northern California, approximately 35 miles south of San Francisco and 20 miles north of San Jose.  Stanford University is in the heart of Northern California's dynamic "Silicon Valley," home to Yahoo!, Google, Hewlett-Packard, and many other cutting edge companies that were started by and continue to be led by Stanford alumni and faculty. This environment provides unparalleled access to a wide variety of opportunities for students to engage with while attending Stanford and even after completing their training as an alumnus.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing in the first year is guaranteed for most students based on housing availability and meeting the housing application deadline.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
LGBTQ Meds is dedicated to raising awareness of queer health issues and promoting equal social and political rights for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer people.  LGBTQ Meds serves as a support group, safe space, and social group for all medical students, undergraduates, faculty, and staff, regardless of sexual orientation or gender identity, who are interested in queer health issues. The Stanford Medicine curriculum includes 10 hours of specific LGBTQ+ Affirming Healthcare curriculum for medical students, with clinical rotation options for students and other trainees/fellows.   
 
Additionally, Vaden Health Services and The Weiland Health Initiative both offer LGBTQ+ specific student health and mental health resources aligning with WPATH Standards of Care.
 
https://med.stanford.edu/lgbtqmeds.html 
 
https://stanfordhealthcare.org/medical-clinics/lgbtq-health.html 
 
https://med.stanford.edu/pride
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Disability Resources, a division of the Office of Medical Student Affairs is charged with determining eligibility for, facilitating, and supporting implementation of reasonable accommodations for MD and MSPA students at Stanford University School of Medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Office of Medical Student Wellness (OMSW) provides student life advising, wellness programming and learning environment initiatives to enable students to thrive academically and personally throughout their medical school experience. Our aim is to foster a safe and supportive learning environment.   Students are encouraged to bring issues that impact their life decisions, well-being, and academic performance to OMSW.   We provide information on resources throughout the university that can support students through any challenges they may be facing.  For more detailed information about services, visit the OMSW website. 
https://med.stanford.edu/md/student-wellness.html

OMSW works closely with the Mental Health Team (MHT) which provides free and accessible mental health care to School of Medicine and Bioscience students. Learn about their services and meet the team at the MHT website. https://med.stanford.edu/mht.html
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo:
To provide medical students with the opportunity to learn medicine in a variety of settings, students are responsible for their own transportation to and from Stanford and its affiliated sites and are expected to arrive on time, which may require advance planning. 

Students are responsible for making appropriate travel arrangements and all costs associated with travel to their assigned clinical sites unless they exceed the 50-mile one-way local area as defined by Stanford policy.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Support through advising deans, clinical and research mentors, wellness programs, student life advisor, mental health team, learning specialist, and the clerkship focused Student Guidance Program.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Opportunities within the curriculum begin first quarter. Early Clinical Exp. provides patient contact via lens of the clinician. Early Patient Exp. provides patient contact, via lens of the patient.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lecture-based, small group, problem-based learning, flipped classroom, labs, and 1:1 faculty-student clinical experiences starting in the first quarter of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Students must successfully complete all pre-clerkship course requirements and pass a pre-clerkship clinical performance exam prior to beginning clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Stanford offers the Leadership in Health Disparities Program which focuses on addressing national health inequities and provides additional resources to help the student acclimate more effectively.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance at most lectures is optional but encouraged; all lectures recorded. Attendance at lectures involving patients, small group sessions, labs, and the Practice of Medicine course is mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Stanford is committed to ensuring that each graduate has the opportunity to fully explore their potential as a student and as a scholar. Key goals of the curriculum are the melding of 21st century basic science and clinical translation of new discoveries, with critical topics on population health, health equity, and AI threaded throughout the curriculum. Our strong emphasis on patient care is reflected in clinical experiences beginning in the first year, and in the Educators for CARE clinical mentoring program. Opportunity for serious longitudinal scholarly work is enhanced through our Physician Scientist Training program, which includes an option to “split the curriculum” allowing students to complete second year courses over two years, providing opportunity for a more in-depth research experience. All M.D. candidates must satisfactorily complete at least 13 quarters of academic work including the completion of a Scholarly Concentration project as well as the required Transition to Residency course at the end of their clinical year to prepare them for the next phase of their career. 

Explore the Discovery Curriculum:
http://med.stanford.edu/md/discovery-curriculum.html
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Stanford Medicine's educational mission is to prepare physicians who will provide outstanding patient-centered care, and to inspire future leaders who will improve world health through scholarship and innovation . All students are required to successfully complete both Ambulatory Medicine and Family Medicine clerkships, where they work in primary care settings both within Stanford hospitals, and at community-based sites, as well as a required Community Health for the Underserved clinical clerkship that provides an immersive experience caring or the medically underserved within the community.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
At our research-intensive medical school, students have abundant opportunities to conduct cutting-edge research under the direction of world-class faculty members at the school, hospital and clinics, and throughout the University. For over three decades, the Stanford Medical Scholars Research Program has provided logistical and financial support directly to students, totaling over $3,000,000 this past year, for medical student research on campus and at multiple locations abroad. Research opportunities include diverse areas for student scholarly work, including the basic medical sciences, clinical/translational studies, clinical trials, public health/public policy studies, medical education, medical humanities, and social justice and health equity. For a full list, see:

http://med.stanford.edu/md/student-research/scholarly-concentrations.html
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Opportunities for community-engaged service, education, and scholarship are widely available and encouraged. All students complete at least three sessions at the Cardinal Free Clinics.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText:
Completion of a scholarly project is required through one of the Scholarly Concentrations.

http://med.stanford.edu/md/student-research/scholarly-concentrations.html
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Stanford Hospital and Clinics; Lucile Packard Children's Hospital; Santa Clara County Valley Medical Center; Palo Alto Veterans’ Administration Hospital; Kaiser Permanente Medical Center, Santa Clara.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pre-clerkship coursework is graded pass/fail. Clerkship rotations are graded using a criterion-based Pass With Distinction in six domains of medical practice.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Stanford University sits on the ancestral land of the Muwekma Ohlone tribe.

In 1858, the Cooper Medical College in San Francisco was founded by Dr. Elias Samuel Cooper as the first medical school on the Pacific Coast.  In 1908, Stanford University adopted the Cooper Medical College as its medical school and moved it to the Stanford campus in 1959. 

Stanford Medicine seeks to inspire and prepare a diverse group of exceptional physician scientists, scholars, and leaders to transform human health across all communities through pioneering research and discovery, innovative education, and compassionate patient-centered healthcare.

The Stanford School of Medicine is consistently ranked in the top ten of all research university medical centers in the country.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Accepted candidates receiving offers on or prior to April 30 are permitted up to two weeks to acknowledge receipt of the offer.  Offers made after this date are permitted two to five days.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
A minimum of 3 and maximum of 6 individual letters of recommendation is required. All LORs must be written on official letterhead and signed by the recommender(s) or committee members.

Pre-medical committee evaluations/letters are not required. However, if submitted, only the individual letters contained within the pre-medical committee packet will count towards the number of letters of recommendation. If the committee evaluation/letter references or summarizes individual evaluators, each individual evaluation/letter of recommendation must be included in the committee packet.
Examples: 
(1) If a committee evaluation/letter is submitted containing 4 individual letters, the letters of recommendation requirement is fulfilled.  Up to 2 additional letters may be submitted.

(2) If one committee evaluation/letter is submitted containing no individual letters, the letters of recommendation requirement is NOT fulfilled. 
 
For more info: http://med.stanford.edu/md-admissions/how-to-apply.html
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
While Stanford Medicine does not have strict specifications of preferred letters of recommendation writers, letters that support the designated meaningful experiences and attest to the following aspects of the applicant's skills and attributes are encouraged:
leadership
originality and creativity
innovation
research skills and independence
pursuit of scholarship
clinical exposures and caring experiences
cultural humility
health equity and advocacy
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: In addition to candidate assessment, presentations include curriculum, academic programs, and community engagement opportunities.  Candidates are provided the opportunity to engage with current students through coordinated social activities (virtually).
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Hybrid MMI (Multiple Mini Interview and Traditional Interview)
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All eligible applicants. Stanford Med has a strict no-transfer policy and reserves the right to deny a supplemental application to those who have previously enrolled in another medical school.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Stanford Medicine is committed to diversity in its operations and programs in all dimensions, in conformance with the law, and seeks to admit a diverse body of students who are interested in the intellectual substance of medicine and are committed to advancing scholarship in any field of medicine. Desirable candidates for admissions are academically ready to succeed in our curriculum, have life experiences that will enrich our learning environment, and have personal qualities that will serve them, their colleagues, and their patients well in their professional lives.

Applicants must have received a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university by the time of enrollment. They are encouraged to explore diverse educational opportunities throughout their college careers and undergo rigorous preparation in the life sciences. Stanford students have demonstrated a sustained commitment to scholarship in an area of their interest.

In our flexible consideration of diverse curricular backgrounds of our students, Stanford Medicine does not have specific course requirements, but instead recommends coursework and experiences that generate depth of knowledge in biology, chemistry and physics, mathematics, behavioral and social sciences, communication, and laboratory or field experiments.

Other details on admissions policies are available on our website: https://med.stanford.edu/md-admissions/admissions-policies.html
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores are considered along with other metrics in the assessment of academic readiness. These metrics are used  without rigid numerical cut-offs in the context of holistic admissions.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: There is no minimum undergraduate GPA for consideration.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: There is no minimum number of credit hours for consideration.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept coursework completed at a community college and will review these grades along with all other grades from a candidate's baccalaureate work as well as any postbaccalaureate or graduate coursework completed at the time of application.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
Updates to an application will be accepted only after an applicant has been invited to interview and no later than one week after the interview date. 

Letters of Intent may be submitted near the CYMS date in April.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
A candidate for the MD degree at Stanford School of Medicine must demonstrate the capacity to acquire the knowledge, attitudes, and skills necessary to complete the MD Program educational requirements, including those set forth in the School of Medicine Technical Standards. Graduates will achieve the MD Program competencies in the basic and clinical sciences, and they will be able to graduate as skilled and effective practitioners of medicine with or without reasonable accommodations.

Stanford SoM intends for its graduates to become competent and compassionate physicians who are capable of entering residency training and meeting all requirements for medical licensure. The goal is to develop deep foundational knowledge of medicine, the ability to apply outstanding clinical skills, effective and efficient data interpretation skills, and clinical decision making across a broad spectrum of medical situations in all settings.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Stanford Medicine Office of Financial Aid policy is rooted in the philosophy that students, with the help of their families, have the primary responsibility for financing their medical education to the fullest extent of their estimated ability.  Stanford Medicine is committed to providing students financial support commensurate with the calculated financial need. Stanford Medicine requires parent and student financial resource information from ALL students applying for need-based, institutional (Stanford Medicine) scholarship and loan funding. International students are eligible for institutional need-based grant and loans but must provide certification of finances for cost of attendance not covered by financial aid.

medSchoolPrograms.info: Additional programs including MD/PhD; MD/MA; MD/MS described at http://med.stanford.edu/education/dual-degree-programs.html

The Postbaccalaureate Experience in Research provides research and training opportunities to enable scholars to become successful graduate or medical students. We aim to create a pipeline into higher education for scholars with demonstrated potential in STEMM and health related fields. 

The Physician Scientist Training Program (PSTP) focuses on applicants considering careers as physician scientists. Students combine preclinical coursework with an opportunity for longitudinal research (basic science or clinical), through 3 different pathways: (1) splitting the second-year curriculum over two years, (2) taking a full year of research (usually after the second-year) or (3) through a 2-year dedicated lab experience (Berg Scholars Program), each supplemented with physician-scientist-specific career development. 

http://med.stanford.edu/pstp
http://med.stanford.edu/md/discovery-curriculum/BergScholarsProgram

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: After April 30, offers of admission are made from the waitlist of acceptable candidates until the class size is filled.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: In our flexible consideration of diverse curricular backgrounds of our students, Stanford Medicine does not have specific course requirements, but instead recommends coursework and experiences that generate depth of knowledge in biology, chemistry and physics, mathematics, behavioral and social sciences, communication, and laboratory or field experiments.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants are selected based on their academic readiness, relevant life experiences, and personal qualities, taking into account their educational context. Stanford University admits qualified students of any race, color, national or ethnic origin, sex, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, and gender identity, veteran status, or marital status to all the rights, privileges, programs, and activities generally accorded or made available to students at the University.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing is recommended although we value any exposure to the medical field through a number of avenues including work and volunteering experiences. Our main aim is that the candidate has experience within healthcare such that they can knowledgeably speak to their decision to pursue medical education and the rigors required as part of medical training and practice.
